EOMasters Newsletter #019

10/03/2024

Hello EO-Masters!

another 2 weeks have passed, and I provide you a newselection of handpicked news.

This week I wrote a new blog. It started as a distraction from my daily work. I wanted to do something different and it ended up in a video, an animation and this blog. It's about the project The Line. I recently stumbled across it again and thought it would be interesting to see what the current status is.

Now let's go on with the latest news.

Ciao

Marco

The Line - A Look at the Mega Project

This blog started as distraction from the daily work. I wanted to do something different, and it ended in a video and this blog. The project is shortly introduced and discussed. In the video we fly along the construction site of The Line using Copernicus data.

  • The Line - A Look at the Mega Project

EO and RS News

FDR4ALT - Innovative Data Records from Old Instruments

ESA released the Fundamental Data Records for Altimetry project - FDR4ALT. The new records, available in NetCDF format, are derived from the ERS-1, ERS-2 and Envisat Altimeter and Radiometer instruments. The data sets are to be used for the long-term utilisation of data on the various Earth surfaces: Ocean, coastal waters, inland waters, ice sheets, sea ice and atmosphere.

  •  FDR4ALT - ESA unveils new cutting-edge ERS/Envisat Altimeter and Microwave Radiometer Datasets

  • FDR4ALT – Fundamental Data Records for Altimetry

Swarm: 10 Success Stories in 10 Years

In this article, ESA highlights ten success stories of the Swarm mission that have been achieved in 10 years of being in orbit. This includes Swarm FAST data, Swarm’s Essential Planetary Variable, Swarm data in your smartphone and others.

  •  Magnetic magic: 10 reasons to be excited about Swarm

An In-Depth Look at the Copernicus Arctic Hub

The Arctic is warming four times faster than the rest of the world, disrupting ecosystems and attracting geo-economic interest due to navigable waters and natural resources.

The Copernicus Arctic Hub provides access to over 150 Earth Observation products for climate, ocean, land, and emergency issues in the Arctic.

The article provides an in-depth look at the platform.

  • OBSERVER: An in-depth look at the Copernicus Arctic Hub

Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem Wants Your Feedback

In preparation for the User Review Meeting, the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem needs your feedback. In a 10-question survey you can help to improve the service.

And ten of you can win a year-long subscription with an additional 10,000 monthly credits.

  • User Review Survey | Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem

Software, Tools and Services

HYPERNETS MDB from Sentinel data for the validation of satellite water products

The HYPERNETS project aims to develop a new, cost-effective hyperspectral radiometer called HYPSTAR, along with an associated pointing system and an embedded calibration device. Quality controlled data with uncertainty estimates are processed automatically by the HYPERNETS PROCESSOR, supporting the validation of all optical satellite missions.

Match-up Database (MDB) files for the validation of satellite water products from Sentinel-3 OLCI and Sentinel-2 MSI have recently been released.

  • HYPERNETS.eu

  • Match-up Database (MDB) files for the validation of satellite water products from Sentinel-3 OLCI and Sentinel-2 MSI using the initial samples of HYPERNETS in situ data (zenodo.org)

  • HYPERNETS Processor: Processor for Hypernets field data to generate the user products

Beyond EO

Extracting Gold from E-Waste, with Cheese

Scientist have developed a process which is able to extract gold from e-waste using cheese. More precisely they use, among other things, a protein fibre sponge that they produce from whey. Whey is a by-product of the cheese-making process.

According to the researchers, the cost of procuring the raw materials plus the energy cost of the entire process is 50 times less than the value of the gold that can be extracted from it.

  • Using cheese waste to recover gold from electronic waste

Tschüss and Goodbye!

Marco
